decisions.statement: The pages carried on are the pages of that page type and of every page type beneath that type.
Which pages carry the key is read from the values the index files for each page type.
No page body is read to find out which pages carry the key.
A page type with no property under either key is refused.
A run over one key answers where those pages sit rather than what each holds.
A run over one key reaches a key the page type no longer declares.
A page type the index does not name is refused.
A page with no value under the key read from is passed over rather than refused.
A page already with the key written to is passed over rather than refused.
A list holding one value becomes that value where the key written to has one value.
A list holding more than one value is refused where the key written to has one value.
The value is handed on as the body spells that value rather than as text to quote.
A count handed in holds how many pages are carried on.
A run handed no count carries on every page with the key read from.
A count that is no whole number above nothing is refused.
The arguments a run of either shape takes are named here rather than by a caller.
Nothing here says which mechanical changes a page is carried through.
Nothing here works out a body of its own.

definition: which pages of a page type hold a key, and carrying that value under a second key
